title: Fallen Survey Line
description: A surviving foot and three split shaft drums along one fall line, ending in a broken cushion capital.

review.notes: Round 1 of the new budget, judged against the PR #6 round-3 notes. Better: the gear-wheel slots are gone, there is a fall line of drums ending in a capital, and the drums sit in turf (hero.jpg, closeup_base). Still failing: the flutes are now convex rounded ribs, so every drum reads as corrugated sheet or a pleated paper lantern, the same fault as round 1 of PR #6 (closeup_upper). Fix: concave Doric flutes cut into the drum with sharp arrises between them, matching column_white_a. Break faces: the fracture surfaces are coarse crumpled triangulation like crushed foil (closeup_base). Fix: a few large conchoidal fracture planes with crisp edges and small secondary chips. Capital: the cushion capital is a smooth featureless form with a round drilled hole on its face; give it a profiled echinus, an abacus with a broken corner, and remove the hole. Material: clean uniform white everywhere; add grime where the drums meet the ground and lichen on the up-facing sides.
